what: The charter tool's held instance under codemother — one address written in two roots: this folder carries the instance's declared assembly; ~/.cairn/devices/codemother/0/tools/charter/ carries its life (the data_recorder backpack at inbound/, built directly by codemother's shim with no declaration file).
why: Charter is a tool and a tool has users, not an owner (Law 6) — but a tool INSTANCE needs a holder, and the holder is the one whose feedback loop can act on it. Charter is a building tool; build-quality feedback belongs to the builder, and codemother owns the care of the code. Before this placement charter's own probe posted findings to 'charter' flat and nothing received them (undelivered 0bfd6e268f73). This is the first code ownership transfer from CC to another device (ticket 65b34c57ab71).

backpack.declaration: none — codemother's shim builds it at charter_backpack()

assembly.ensured_by: cairn.devices.codemother.shim.ensure_charter_instance — on activate and on the charter verb
assembly.reached_by: codemother's charter and feedback verbs; only devices are on the bus, so nothing posts to the instance by name (outline 19.16)

gates: none of its own — the holder gates; the instance is a backpack codemother's verbs write into and a reader drains
falsifier: RED if the instance gates writes at its own address or gains glue that interfaces with charter's operation — then charter has become a machine and the complexity axis was violated (ticket 65b34c57ab71 clause 4).
owner: codemother holds the instance; CC owns the code that assembles it
traces_to: Law 6 — tools have users, not owners; instances have holders
how_it_learns: It does not; the backpack accumulates feedback for a reader (scheduled-llm-gate-inspection when built) — the learning is the reader's.
state_and_history: instance-space only: ~/.cairn/devices/codemother/0/tools/charter/inbound/records.jsonl; no state.json, no history.json — the instance is not a component with a voyage of its own.
